newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura incident seen having limited impact on TSE.
newsitem.headline: Nomura incident seen having limited impact on TSE.

text.p: News of suspected illegal deals involving Nomura Securities executives hurt the brokerage's shares on Friday, but the impact on the overall market was limited and is likely to remain so, analysts said.
They said the market was already split in different directions with financial stocks slipping and multinationals strengthening, adding that the latest revelations were not entirely unexpected.
"It (the news) won't necessarily change the entire market trend," said Shinichi Ichikawa, a strategist at Credit Lyonnais Securities Co Ltd.
For instance, Japanese multinational firms have been rising, backed by solid earnings and the weaker yen.

Some brokers had been concerned that the Nomura scandal, which broke on Thursday after the market closed, might put an overall dampener on stock prices on Friday but the impact proved to be less harmful than feared.
Shares of banks and brokerages have been hurt by the government's "Big Bang" reform plan to liberalise the financial markets.
"Ahead of the financial reforms, weaker firms are likely to see further sales, and it doesn't matter whether we have the news or not," Ichikawa said.
The market's key index, the Nikkei 225 average, fell earlier on Friday on the news but bounced back to close higher at 18,198.74, up 157.41 points or 0.87 percent.
Nomura, however, fell 50 yen to 1,530 yen on Friday, after being ask-only at the opening. Nomura's turnover was heavy at 8.275 million, the second most actively traded stock.
On Thursday, Nomura vice president Atsushi Saito publicly admitted that it was highly likely that two of its directors had been involved in illegal deals.
As for Nomura itself, analysts expect the brokerage's shares to remain weak until the stock market gets an idea of what kind of punishment may be in store for Nomura.
The securities watchdog's investigation was likely to take time, they added.

"Investigations take a long time to complete in the first place and as the market is at a crucial stage ahead of the end-March book closings, punishment measures will probably not be announced or carried out in a hurry," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities.
The Finance Ministry said on Friday morning that it would take any strict measures that are necessary against Nomura after seeing the results of the probe.
Brokers said penalties could come in the form of a partial suspension of Nomura's business and personnel changes, which would not affect customers.
